html:
A Buddhist monastery on Mount Hiei, above Kyoto, founded in 788 by the monk Saichō. It is the head temple of the Tendai school of Japanese Buddhism.

Saichō went to Tang China in 804, in the same embassy as Kūkai, and brought back the Tiantai teaching, which he called Tendai. Because the mountain lay to the northeast of the new capital Heian-kyō, the unlucky direction, the temple was also seen as the city's guardian.

Over the next centuries Enryaku-ji became the great training school of Japanese Buddhism. Founders of the later popular schools studied here: Hōnen of Pure Land, Shinran, Eisai of Rinzai Zen, Dōgen and Nichiren. It also grew into a rich landlord with thousands of armed warrior monks, who marched on the capital to press their demands.

In 1571 Oda Nobunaga burned the whole complex and killed thousands to break its power. It was rebuilt in the 1600s and is now a World Heritage Site.
sum: A Buddhist monastery on Mount Hiei, above Kyoto, founded in 788 by the monk Saichō. It is the head temple of the Tendai school of Japanese Buddhism.
